source.title: AR&D: A Framework for Retrieving and Describing Concepts for Interpreting AudioLLMs
source.authors: T. F. Chowdhury; Ta Duc Huy; Siqi Pan; Jeremy Stoddard; Zhi-Bin Liao

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE-derived features in an AudioLLM, a new setting, using semantic alignment, human assessment, and feature steering. It does not reproduce the original toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: Results cited from prior work and implementation choices such as K=250, p=4, and C=5000 are not study-result rows. The paper reports aggregate metrics for datasets and methods; no per-feature results are given.
record.test_reason: In one AudioLLM (Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct), the study compares TopK-SAE features with raw neuron activations ('Poly. Feats.') on concept alignment, human ratings, steering and monosemanticity. That bears on V4 (an SAE recovers sparse, interpretable features in a real large model) in a new modality. Much of the rest compares the paper's own clip-selection score against variants, which does not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAEs disentangle polysemantic AudioLLM activations into monosemantic features, and that AudioLLMs 'encode structured, interpretable features', validated by human evaluation and steering.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK sparse autoencoders on AudioLLM residual-stream activations, then ranks, names, evaluates, and steers features. It does not use the original toy-network setup or its geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer changes the reported monosemanticity scores, with layer 26 highest; expansion factor changes scores, with only minor reported gains beyond 8. The Happy → Angry steering result is lower than the other AR&D steering tasks.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The authors illustrate the approach on one AudioLLM and focus on a representative decoder layer. Most reported evaluation values have no uncertainty estimates; steering results have no reported uncertainty. The study itself notes a moderate probing dataset and limited Angry samples for one steering task.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 precision and recall values were omitted to keep the record focused on the reported F1, mAP, and monosemanticity measures; Table 1, which states these measures track semantic alignment and interpretability. No separately reported outcomes from the text were otherwise omitted.

untested.parts: No toy model, feature/dimension sweep, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity pressure or feature importance as cause of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not directly measure how features are spread across neurons. Only one model; no other AudioLLMs or text LLMs.
No completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicality tests. The expansion-factor sweep reports only max MS.
No test of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Table 4 AR&D layer 26, e=8 max MS = 9.31 (the default setting) has no row.
Table 1 lists AR&D MS 9.17/9.31/9.33 under l=5/16/26, but these match Table 4's layer-26 e=4/8/16 values. The Table 1 condition labels need checking.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence for V4 is weak in kind. Evaluated features are pre-filtered (top C=5000) by the study's own CLAP-based monosemanticity score, and both MS and the F1/mAP metrics rely on CLAP, so the metrics are not independent. 'Highest MS' is a maximum, not a typical value. There is one model, no uncertainty on steering, and an LLM judge. Rows R03-R08 compare clip-selection scores within the pipeline and do not bear on V4. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment, feature-over-dimension sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular-geometry measurement.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether more important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.
Tests whether SAE features can be recovered and interpreted in one AudioLLM; does not measure feature spread across neurons or test other AudioLLMs.
Does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses scalar SAE latent dimensions but does not test whether represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
